nodes.statement: For notational convenience, we assume C=emptyset. Fix (T_0,T_1) and T as in Theorem . By Proposition , we may assume that T is stable (for every xinomega, either xrightarrow_T y for all but finitely many y, or yrightarrow_T x for all but finitely many y). In the rest of the proof, every Turing functional Phi^G is computing a set of integers, namely \n: Phi^G(n)downarrow =1\; so it makes sense to write Phi^Gcap A. Let A_0sqcup A_1 be a 2-partition (of omega) such that xin A_0 if and only if xrightarrow_T y for all but finitely many yin omega (which is well defined since T is stable). This automatically ensures that xin A_1 iff yrightarrow_T x for all but finitely many yinomega. For a set Zsubseteq omega, a 2-partition X_0sqcup X_1 of omega, we say Z is compatible with X_0sqcup X_1 if Zcap X_0rightarrow_T Zcap X_1. Note that if Zsubseteq X_i for some i, then Z is compatible\ with X_0sqcup X_1. A condition is a Mathias condition (F,X) with the following properties: item [(a)] F is T-transitive and compatible\ with A_0sqcup A_1; item [(b)] Fcap A_0rightarrow_T Xrightarrow_T Fcap A_1; item [(c)] (T_0,T_1) is X-4-hyperimmune. A precondition is a Mathias condition satisfying (a)(c). Let (F,X) be a condition and Ysubseteq X. item If Y is T-transitive, then Fcup Y is T-transitive. item If Y is compatible\ with A_0sqcup A_1, then Fcup Y is compatible\ with A_0sqcup A_1. item For every precondition (E,Y), there is a binomega so that (E,Ycap (b,infty)) is a condition. Item (1)(2) follows from property (b) of (F,X). Item (3) follows from definition of A_0,A_1. For every condition (F, X) there exists an extension (E, Y) such that |E| > |F|. Let xin Xsmallsetminus F. Clearly \x\ is T-transitive and compatible\ with A_0sqcup A_1. By Lemma item (1)(2), (Fcup\x\, X) is a precondition. For einomega, iin 2, let R_e^i denote the requirement: Phi_e^G is not a solution to T_i. We will construct a solution G of T satisfying: R_e_0,e_1: R_e_0^0vee R_e_1^1 for all e_0,e_1inomega. A condition (F,X) forces R_e_0,e_1 if: for every solution G of T satisfying (F,X), G satisfies R_e_0,e_1. Note that the definition of forcing is slightly different from that in section , that we restrict to T-transitive set. This restriction cannot be applied in section since there we deal with arbitrary instance instead of computable instance. For every condition c and indices e_0,e_1inomega, there is an extension of c forcing R_e_0,e_1. Fix c=(D,X). By Lemma , for notational convenience, we assume D=emptyset and X=omega. We firstly describe a process to partially compute a 4-array. Then we show that if the computation diverges, we obtain an extension dleq c forcing R_e_0,e_1 in the Pi_1^0 way: one of Phi_e_i^G is not infinite; and if the computation converges, we obtain dleq c forcing R_e_0,e_1 in a Sigma_1^0 way: for some n,m,l so that T_0,T_1 diagonalizes against\ (V_n,V_n,m), (U_n,m,U_n,m,l) respectively, either Phi_e_0^Gcap U_nneemptysetwedgePhi_e_0^Gcap U_n,mneemptyset; or Phi_e_1^Gcap V_n,mneemptysetwedgePhi_e_1^Gcap V_n,m,lneemptyset (which means for some i<2, Phi_e_i^G is not a solution to T_i). Given n,minomega, search computably for some finite set U_n,m>m, V_n,m>n such that for every 4-partition X_0sqcupcdotssqcup X_3: item [(a)] either there exists an i< 4, a finite T-transitive set Esubseteq X_i such that Phi_e_0^Ecap U_n neq emptyset and Phi_e_0^Ecap U_n,mneemptyset; item [(b)] or there exist jne i<4 and two finite T-transitive sets Fsubseteq X_j, Esubseteq X_i such that Phi_e_0^Ecap U_n neq emptyset and Phi_e_1^Fcap V_n,mneemptyset. This is straightforward. For a set $Z\subseteq \omega$, a $2$-partition

$4$-array. Then we show that if the computation
diverges, we obtain an extension $d\leq c $ forcing $\mathcal{R}_{e_0,e_1}$
in the $\Pi_1^0$ way: one of $\Phi_{e_i}^{G}$ is not infinite; and if the computation converges,
we obtain $d\leq c$ forcing $\mathcal{R}_{e_0,e_1}$ in a
$\Sigma_1^0$ way: for some $n,m,l$ so that
$T_0,T_1$ diagonalizes against\ $(V_n,V_{n,m}), (U_{n,m},U_{n,m,l})$ respectively,
either $\Phi_{e_0}^G\cap U_n\ne\emptyset\wedge\Phi_{e_0}^G\cap U_{n,m}\ne\emptyset$;
or $\Phi_{e_1}^G\cap V_{n,m}\ne\emptyset\wedge\Phi_{e_1}^G\cap V_{n,m,l}\ne\emptyset$
(which means for some $i<2$,  $\Phi_{e_i}^G$ is not a solution to $T_i$).

Given $n \in \omega$, search computably for some
finite set $U_n>n$ such that
for every $8$-partition
  $X_0\sqcup\cdots\sqcup X_7 = \omega$, there exists an $i< 8$,
  a finite $T$-transitive set $E\subseteq X_i$
  such that  $\Phi_{e_0}^E\cap U_n\ne\emptyset $.
\smallskip

 \emph{Defining $U_{n,m},V_{n,m}$}.
 Given $n,m\in\omega$, search computably for some
 finite set $U_{n,m}>m, V_{n,m}>n$
such that
for every $4$-partition $X_0\sqcup\cdots\sqcup X_3$:
\begin{itemize}
\item [(a)]  either there exists an $i< 4$, a finite $T$-transitive set $E\subseteq X_i$
   such that   $\Phi_{e_0}^{E}\cap U_n \neq \emptyset$ and $\Phi_{e_0}^E\cap U_{n,m}\ne\emptyset$;
  \item [(b)] or there exist $j\ne i<4$ and two finite $T$-transitive
  sets $F\subseteq X_j, E\subseteq X_i$ such that
  $\Phi_{e_0}^E\cap U_n \neq \emptyset$ and $\Phi_{e_1}^{F}\cap V_{n,m}\ne\emptyset$.
  \end{itemize}



 \emph{Defining $U_{n,m,l},V_{n,m,l}$}.
  Given $n,m\in\omega$, search computably for some
 finite sets $U_{n,m,l}>m, V_{n,m,l}>l$
 such that for every $2$-partition $X_0\sqcup X_1$, there exists a   finite $T$-transitive set $E $ compatible with $X_0\sqcup X_1$
  such that:
  \begin{itemize}

  \item [(p)] either   $\Phi_{e_0}^E\cap U_n \neq \emptyset$ and $\Phi_{e_0}^E\cap U_{n,m,l}\ne\emptyset$;

  \item [(q)] or
  $\Phi_{e_1}^E\cap V_{n,m} \neq \emptyset$ and $\Phi_{e_1}^E\cap V_{n,m,l}\ne\emptyset$.

By compactness, the following $\Pi_1^0$ class $\mathcal{P}$

there exists a  member

so that $(T_0,T_1)$ is $\oplus_{i<8} X_i$-4-hyperimmune.

\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)]  for every $i< 4$, every finite $T$-transitive set $E\subseteq X_i$,

 $8$-partition $(X_i\cap A_k: i<4,k<2)$. By definition of

 $E\subseteq X_i\cap A_k$,

$X_i$ is finite.

for every $T$-transitive set $G\subseteq X_j$,

$\Phi_{e_1}^G\cap (n,\infty)=\emptyset$.

the  definition of $U_{n,m},V_{n,m}$ (where we take the 4-partition to be $(X_j\cap A_k:j,k<2)$

$$\Phi_{e_0}^E\cap U_n,

forces
$\mathcal{R}_{e_0,e_1}$. Suppose now $X_{\hat j}$ is infinite. Then, taking $d = (F, X_{\hat j})$, a similar argument shows that by property (q) of $X_0\sqcup X_1$, for every  $T$-transitive set $G $  satisfying $d$,

forces
$\mathcal{R}_{e_0,e_1}$. Thus we are done in this subcase.

Both  $X_j$, $X_{\hat j}$ are finite.

If j=hat j=1 (so X_0 is infinite) and hat k=1, k=0, then the condition (F, X_0 smallsetminus [0, b]) forces R_e_1^1 by a similar argument using property (q) of X_0sqcup X_1. \ \\ Case 4: U_n,U_n,m,V_n,m,U_n,m,l,V_n,m,l is found for all n,m,l. Since (T_0,T_1) is 4-hyperimmune, there exist n, m,l such that T_0 and T_1 diagonalize against\ (U_n,U_n,m,l) and (V_n, m,V_n, m,l), respectively. By definition of U_n,m,l,V_n,m,l (where we take X_0sqcup X_1 to be A_0sqcup A_1), there exists a finite T-transitive set F compatible with A_0sqcup A_1 such that item[(p)] either Phi_e_0^Fcap U_n neq emptyset and Phi_e_0^Fcap U_n,m,lneemptyset; item[(q)] or Phi_e_1^Fcap V_n,m neq emptyset and Phi_e_1^Fcap V_n,m,lneemptyset. Let d=(F,X). We claim that d forces R_e_0,e_1 by forcing R^0_e_0 on case (p) and R^1_e_1 on case (q). Let G be a set satisfying d. In the case (p), Phi_e_0^G has a non-empty intersection with both U_n and U_n,m,l, in which case Phi_e_0^G is not a solution to T_0 (recall the definition of diagonalizes against); and in the case (q), Phi_e_1^G has non-empty intersection with both V_n,m and V_n,m,l, in which case Phi_e_1^G is not a solution to T_1. This completes the proof of the lemma.
